prompts.name: properties-for-java-app
prompts.prompt: I have an existing `application.properties` file for a Spring Boot app. I want it as a ConfigMap in ConfigHub, mounted into the container at /etc/app/application.properties. Walk me through it.
prompts.expected_output: Treats ‘Walk me through it’ as coached/educational intent: reads existing state if permitted, explains the rendered file key/mount path, and lays out exact AppConfig/Properties Unit, render-configmap Invocation, Upsert link, ConfigMap placeholder, and workload mount steps with --change-desc where supported. It makes zero mutation calls and clearly labels the user-terminal handoff; if the user later asks the agent to perform a step, that exact step goes separately through the host permission system.

prompts.name: envfrom-env-injection
prompts.prompt: Our Node app reads 15 env vars. I have them all in a `.env` file. I want them injected via `envFrom` in the Deployment so I don't list them individually in the container spec. How?
prompts.expected_output: Prepares an AppConfig/Env Unit and render-configmap proposal using key/value rendering, plus an exact Deployment envFrom change. Calls out SecretStore handling for sensitive values, binds source and Unit identities, does not execute, and includes read-only verification.

prompts.name: mutable-vs-immutable-choice
prompts.prompt: I'm confused about immutable vs mutable ConfigMaps in ConfigHub. We have a legacy monitoring tool that greps for ConfigMaps by exact name — is that a reason to pick one over the other? Also, if the ConfigMap content changes, which mode gives us an automatic pod restart?
prompts.expected_output: Explains the tradeoff: the exact-name consumer supports a stable mutable ConfigMap; the content-hash pod-template annotation is what triggers a rollout for stable names, while immutable hashed names require reference updates. Produces a choice/proposal only and does not mutate.
